parameters.content:
## ppwr-vendor-form

The questionnaire the supplier sees.

**Page 1 asks for nothing.** A Form Trigger renders its first page before any node runs, so there is no way to check the token first. Page 1 carries a hidden token and one confirmation box. Somebody following a dead link clicks once and gets a neutral page. Nothing is asked for and nothing leaks.

**Then two checks.** The signature proves we minted the token. `sha256(token)` against the stored hash proves it is the live one. Either failing gives the same neutral page, so probing the difference tells you nothing.

**Page 2 is generated from the ruleset.** Fields come from `field_catalogue`, so adding a question means editing one JSON file.

**Uploads are recorded before anything is validated.** The submission row is written as `writing`, each file goes to `ppwr-evidence` and gets a `document` row pointing at the address it landed on, and only then does the submission flip to `committed`.

Bytes first, row second. A row whose file never landed is a dangling reference; a file with no row is garbage a sweep can pick up. A submission left at `writing` looks half finished, which is what it is.

### Verify

Decode, re-sign, re-hash, look up. Nothing about the item is read out of the token. It only says which row to fetch.

values.fieldLabel: I am authorised to complete this declaration for my company

nodes.name: Vendor questionnaire (page 1: identity)
nodes.notes: Asks for nothing, so an invalid token cannot leak anything. The Art. 50 interaction line is in the description because a supplier filling in a packaging form has no other way to know a model will read their upload.

nodes.name: Load campaign item by token hash
nodes.notes:
Looked up by hash, not by the id inside the token. A token whose id was tampered with will not match any stored hash.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

parameters.completionTitle: This link is no longer available
parameters.completionMessage:
Please ask your contact at the buying company for a new link.

If you believe this is a mistake, reply to the email that brought you here.

nodes.name: Link no longer available
nodes.notes: One neutral page for every failure. Expired, forged, reissued and already closed all look identical from outside.

nodes.name: Transition to opened
nodes.notes:
Soft: a supplier who opens the form twice is not an error, and the second transition is a no-op the state machine refuses.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Insert submission
nodes.notes:
Written as commit_state 'writing' first. It becomes 'committed' once the documents are attached, so a half written submission is visible as one instead of passing for complete.

Mode is 'each'.

value.transition: ={{ { campaign_item_id: $('Assemble submission').first().json.campaign_item_id, submission_id: $('Split uploaded files').first().json.submission_id, to_state: 'submitted', event_type: 'submission_received', actor: 'vendor', payload: { revision: $('Assemble submission').first().json.revision, answered_fields: $('Assemble submission').first().json.answered_fields } } }}

nodes.name: Screen the submission
nodes.notes:
Started, not waited for. Screening reads documents through a model and can take a while, and a supplier who has finished the form should not be watching a spinner for it.

The submission is already durable at this point: rows written, documents stored, state moved to 'submitted'. If 03 fails, the error handler moves the item to 'error' and an operator hears about it, instead of the supplier seeing a stack trace on a thank you page.

parameters.completionMessage:
Thank you. We will come back to you only if something is missing or inconsistent.

This submission has been screened for completeness and internal consistency. That is not a conformity assessment, and it does not confirm that your packaging conforms to any regulation.

nodes.name: Upload to Base64
nodes.notes: Base64 and not binary crosses the sub-workflow boundary, so this workflow never handles binary plumbing on behalf of the evidence store.

nodes.name: Store evidence
nodes.notes:
The bytes are written before the row that points at them. A document row whose file never landed is a dangling reference; a file with no row is garbage that a sweep can collect.

Content addressed. A resubmission that re-attaches an unchanged document resolves to the same address, so the same bytes are never filed twice.

Mode is 'each'. The evidence store answers one request per call.

value.data: ={{ { submission_id: $json.submission_id, doc_type: $json.doc_type, filename: $json.filename, mime_type: $json.mime_type, byte_size: $json.byte_size, sha256: $json.sha256, storage_uri: $json.storage_uri } }}

nodes.name: Record document
nodes.notes:
The row is the durable record: filename, measured size, content hash, and the address the bytes were written to.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

nodes.name: Mark submission committed
nodes.notes:
Promoted only once every document row exists. A submission stuck at 'writing' is a half written one, and the integrity scan treats it as a failure instead of as data.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

nodes.name: Consume the revision
nodes.notes:
The allocator moves on as soon as a revision is used. Without this a supplier answering a gap notice writes revision 1 again, the upsert overwrites what they sent the first time, and 'a resubmission is a new revision, nothing is overwritten' stops being true.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.
